cases.prompt: We scoped a predictive quality alert for one line. The vendor wants real-time streaming and a full analytics platform. Before we write the business case, does that fit what the plant actually has? (fictional)
cases.expected_output: Rates the complexity drivers for the problem, not the solution, and counts only high or dominant ones. Names the candidate focus areas and compares as-is with target with evidence. Runs the evaluation script and pastes its output with a score. States one of the four verdicts and an owner for each gap. Does not approve any investment.

cases.prompt: The requester set every IT/OT target to the highest level because the platform supports it. Is that fine?
cases.expected_output: Says a target above as-is needs a named driver or business need, and that platform support is no reason. Flags targets with no high or dominant driver as over-engineered. Proposes lowering the targets or naming the missing business need. Notes the architecture-choice areas are not a ladder.

cases.prompt: All levels look fine for this tool, but nobody owns it and there is no support level defined. Can we mark it ready to build? (fictional)
cases.expected_output: Says no: a tool without an operations concept (owner, service level, support level) is never ready to build. Gives the verdict escalate and routes it to the decision-rights skill. Puts the tool boundary sentence and concept status next to the verdict.

cases.prompt: Give me an as-is maturity profile of this one packaging machine on the 16 IT/OT areas, with evidence per level. (fictional)
cases.expected_output: Uses the absorbed maturity profile procedure rather than a use-case fit evaluation. Rates each area qualitatively with an evidence grade and source. Does not rate from the top of the scale. Produces a profile record and a route signal, not a verdict on investment.

cases.prompt: Calculate the annual saving and payback for this use case so we can request budget.
cases.expected_output: Recognises this as value and cost work, not solution-fit evaluation. Points to the business-case skills instead of running the focus-area evaluation.

should_trigger: Does this envisioned solution fit what the plant has, or is it over-engineered?
Rank our use case against known configurations and score the gaps
Which IT/OT capability areas does this use case depend on and what is missing at the plant?
The target is set as high as possible, check if that is justified
should_not_trigger: Write the one-page definition of this new use case
Work out the payback and savings ledger rows for this use case
Check whether the signals for this use case are available on the platform
Derive the acceptance criteria and write the epic and stories
